question: GQ-002
metric: output tokens returned per 1,000 billed input tokens — a direct read on effectiveness per unit of compute
interpretation: The spread tracks caching, not model capability. CodexOpenAI caches 97.2% of its input and returns 85.86 output tokens per 1k billed; MiniMax caches 0% and returns 25.09 despite being the designated cheap lane. Turning caching on where it is off is a larger multiplier than any model swap available here.
caveat: Output tokens are a proxy for useful work, not a measure of it. A model emitting more tokens is not thereby more effective; this bounds the cost side of the 10x question, not the quality side.
sample_note: CodexProxy showed the highest ratio at 95.55 but on only 4 requests, so a 100-request floor was applied before comparing. Reporting a 4-request outlier as the headline would have been the kind of plausible-looking number this repo exists to catch.
requests_definition: 'requests' counts log rows carrying token accounting (prompt_tokens > 0), not all rows. Verified 2026-08-04: CodexOpenAI has 867 rows at or before the measurement time, of which 459 carry no tokens and 408 do — the asserted figure. Minimax 207/64/143, CodexProxy 54/50/4, all matching. The field name alone implied total requests, which would have made every per-request average wrong by ~2x.

providers.1.raw_input.query: select sum(prompt_tokens) from logs where provider='CodexOpenAI' and timestamp <= '2026-08-04 04:19:50';
